s-base.title: Back to the centre
s-base.lesson: In singles you cover the whole court alone: after every shot, go back to the centre.

steps.q: You play a high clear into the middle of the opponent's back court. Tap where you go now.

why.best: To the base position in the centre, slightly behind the middle of your half. From there you reach all four corners in a few steps.
why.good: Almost. Move more to the centre so all corners are the same distance away.

s-receive.title: Receiving in singles
s-receive.lesson: In singles you receive further back than in doubles, because high, long serves are normal.

steps.q: A is ready to serve. You receive in your right service court. Tap where you should stand.

why.best: About 1 to 1.5 metres behind the short service line, near the centre line. In singles many serves are high and long; from here you reach them and a short serve too.
why.good: Almost. In singles you stand a bit further back than in doubles, but not on the baseline.

s-serve.title: Serving in singles
s-serve.lesson: In singles the high, long serve is safe: your opponent has to go all the way to the baseline.

steps.q: You serve in singles from the right. A stands in the middle of his service court. Which serve?
opts: High, long serve
The shuttle drops almost vertically at the baseline. A has to go right to the back and can hardly attack.
Short serve to the T
Also good, especially against players who love to smash. It has to skim the tape, though.
High serve to the mid-court
Too short: A is already under it and can attack straight away.
Short serve wide
Opens an angle for A, and a small error quickly lands out.

s-late.title: Late at the back
s-late.lesson: Red light in singles: play high and deep to buy time to get back to the centre.

steps.q: A pushes you into your back backhand corner. You arrive late and the shuttle is already low.
opts: High, deep clear to the middle
High and deep gives you the most time to get back to the centre. Played to the middle, A has little angle.
High straight clear
Also safe. But if it falls short, A has the whole diagonal open.
Backhand drop
From here the drop often floats too high, and A is close enough to attack it.
Backhand smash
From low behind you, the smash has no power or angle, and you cannot get back in time.

s-net.title: After your net shot
s-net.lesson: After a tight net shot, go back only to just in front of the centre: a smash is impossible from there, a net duel is not.

steps.q: You play a tight net shot to the opponent's forehand corner. Tap where you go now.

why.best: To the centre, but a little further forward than usual. A has to hit from below: either a net shot back or a lift. From here you reach both.
why.good: Right direction. Stay a little further forward; A cannot smash from this position.

s-away.title: Away from your opponent
s-away.lesson: In singles, play away from your opponent: the diagonal is the longest way.

steps.q: A has played a clear and is still back on the left. You are well under the shuttle.
opts: Drop to the front right
A is back on the left. The front right is the furthest point from him: he has to run across the whole court.
Clear to the other back corner
Sends A across to the back right. Good, but the way is shorter than the diagonal to the front.
Drop to the front left
A only has to run straight forward. Much shorter.
Clear straight at A
Right where A already stands. He can attack without moving.

s-lift.title: After your lift
s-lift.lesson: After your lift, go back to the centre, a little deeper and slightly toward the side of the straight smash.

steps.q: You lift high into A's back corner. He will attack. Tap where you defend.

why.best: Back to the centre, one step deeper than usual and slightly left toward the straight smash. The straight smash is the shortest and fastest.
why.good: Right idea. One step deeper and slightly toward the straight smash.

s-netduel.title: Net duel
s-netduel.lesson: If your opponent is still in the mid-court after his drop, reply with a tight net shot.

steps.q: A plays a drop to your front backhand corner and stays in the mid-court. You reach the shuttle below the tape.
opts: Tight net shot
A is in the mid-court. A tight net shot pulls him forward and usually forces a lift. Then you attack.
High, deep lift
Safe and sends A back. But he can attack.
Cross-court net shot
The long way across the net gives A time to intercept.
Short lift
Too short: A smashes from the mid-court.

s-kill.title: Shuttle above the tape
s-kill.lesson: Above the tape, hit down and away from your opponent.

steps.q: A plays a net shot that floats too high and stays at the net. You meet it above the tape.
opts: Push down to the sideline
Above the tape you can hit down. At the sideline, far from A, it is almost unreachable.
Push to the middle
Also down and behind A. But A only needs one step back.
High lift
You give away the attack and hand A a high shuttle.
Net shot right in front of A
A is right there and plays it straight back down.

s-smash.title: Smashing in singles
s-smash.lesson: In singles, smash to the sideline or at the body, not to the middle.

steps.q: A lifts short to your mid-court. The shuttle is high in front of you and A stands in the middle.
opts: Steep smash to the sideline
In singles A covers the whole court alone. At the sideline he has to reach furthest.
Smash at the body
Hard to return well, but A is right there and can block.
Clear to the back
You waste a high shuttle in the mid-court.
Half-high clear to the mid-court
Too short and too slow: A attacks at once.

s-block.title: Defending the smash
s-block.lesson: Against a smash in singles, block away from the smasher: he has the longest way to the front.

steps.q: A smashes from his back forehand corner to your right side.
opts: Straight block to the net
A is back on the left. The front right is furthest from him; he has to run diagonally forward.
High lift to the other corner
Safe and makes A run, but he can attack again.
Cross-court block
Lands on A's side. He only has to run straight forward.
Half-high lift
Too short: A smashes again right away.

s-after-smash.title: After your smash
s-after-smash.lesson: After a smash in singles, follow in: the block usually comes back short and straight.

steps.q: You smash straight from your back forehand corner. Tap where you go now.

why.best: Forward toward the centre, slightly to the side of your smash. The most common reply is a short, straight block, which you reach early from here.
why.good: Right direction. Move a bit further forward.

receive-stance.title: Ready to receive
receive-stance.lesson: In doubles, receive close to the front and attack the short serve early.

steps.q: A stands at the T and is about to serve. You receive in your right service court. Tap where you should stand.

why.best: Close to the short service line, near the centre line. In doubles most serves are short, so you stand forward to attack them early. From here you can still move back for a flick.
why.good: Almost. Move a bit closer to the short service line and toward the centre line.

short-return.title: Short serve too high
short-return.lesson: Attack the short serve early: if it is above the tape, play flat and down into the mid-court.

steps.q: A serves short, but the shuttle rises a little too high. You are early and meet it above the tape.
opts: Flat push into the mid-court
The shuttle is above the tape, so you play flat and down. A push past the server into the side mid-court forces his partner to hit from below.
Tight net shot
Safe, but you waste the chance to put pressure on right away.
Slow push at the server
The server stands right at the net and easily intercepts a slow push.
High lift to the back
You do not lift the return of a short serve: it hands the attack to your opponents.

front-no-lift.title: Front player on attack
front-no-lift.lesson: Front player on attack: do not lift. Keep the shuttle down with a net shot or a push.

steps.q: Your team is attacking and you are at the front. B blocks your partner's smash short in front of you, below the tape.
opts: Tight net shot
Both opponents are back in defence. A tight net shot pulls them forward and forces a lift, and your partner at the back is ready for it.
Push into the side mid-court
Keeps the pressure on. From below the tape the push rises slightly, though, and can be intercepted.
Cross-court net shot
A long flight along the net gives A time to reach it.
Lift to the back
As the front player on attack you do not lift. It gives away the attack your team just had.

lift-backhand.title: If you must lift
lift-backhand.lesson: If you must lift, lift high and deep, ideally to the back player's backhand corner.

steps.q: A plays a tight net shot to your front backhand corner. You reach it only far below the tape and have to lift.
opts: High cross-court lift to the backhand corner
High and deep, cross-court into the back player's backhand corner. A hard smash is most difficult from there, and you have time to set up side by side.
High straight lift
Also safe, but it lands on the back player's forehand side, where attacking is easier.
Flat attacking lift
A flat lift can surprise, but under pressure A intercepts it easily or B smashes early.
Short lift to the mid-court
Too short: B smashes steeply from close range.

gap-smash.title: The open gap
gap-smash.lesson: Look before you smash: hit the open gap, not the player.

steps.q: A lifts short to the middle of your court. B stands far out near the sideline. Where do you smash?
opts: Smash into the gap between them
B is too far out and the middle is open. A smash into the gap is hard for either of them to reach.
Smash at A's body
Body smashes are strong, but A is ready. The open gap is the better choice.
Drop to the forecourt
With such a high ball in the middle you give away pressure. The smash is stronger here.
Smash to B's sideline
That is exactly where B stands. You play it straight onto his forehand.

flick-return.title: Flick serve
flick-return.lesson: If you reach a flick serve in time, attack it like any other high shuttle.

steps.q: You stand forward to receive, and A flicks the serve over you. You get back in time and the shuttle is high above you.
opts: Steep smash to the middle
If you are there in time, a flick is just a high shuttle. A steep smash to the middle punishes the risky serve.
Fast drop straight
Keeps the attack. Good if you are not fully in position.
Clear to the back
Safe, but you give away the advantage the flick handed you.
Slow cross-court drop
Slow and long in the air: A is still at the front and kills it.

symmetric-def.title: Smash from the middle
symmetric-def.lesson: When the shuttle is in the middle, defend symmetrically: each of you covers one half.

steps.q: You lift from the forecourt right into the middle of their back court. B will smash. Place both of you.

why.best: With the smash coming from the middle, both sides are equally likely. Split the court evenly, side by side at mid depth. You drop back on the right, your partner comes forward on the left.
why.good: Right idea. Stand symmetrically, each in the middle of your half.

net-player-waits.title: The net player is waiting
net-player-waits.lesson: Below the tape with the net player waiting: lift high and deep instead of playing a net shot.

steps.q: A plays a tight net shot to your front forehand corner and stays right at the net. You reach the shuttle far below the tape.
opts: High straight lift to the backhand corner
A is waiting at the net for your net shot. A high, deep lift into B's backhand corner is safe and makes his attack harder.
High cross-court lift
Also safe and deep, but it lands on B's forehand side.
Cross-court net shot
A long flight along the net. A is already at the net and has time to move across.
Straight net shot
Straight into the racket of A, who is waiting at the net.

defend-drop.title: Defending the drop
defend-drop.lesson: If you reach a drop at the net and both opponents are back, reply with a tight net shot.

steps.q: You defend side by side. A plays a slow drop to your forecourt. You reach it just below the tape, and both opponents are back.
opts: Tight net shot
Both opponents are deep. A tight net shot forces one of them forward to lift, and then your team attacks.
High straight lift
Safe, but you stay on defence. Good if you are late.
Push into the mid-court
From below the tape the push rises and lands with B, who can attack it.
Half-high lift
Too short: B smashes from the mid-court.

def-to-attack.title: From defence to attack
def-to-attack.lesson: When your team gets a short lift, switch straight from side by side to front and back.

steps.q: You defend side by side. B lifts short to your side and you will smash straight. Tap where your partner should go now.

why.best: Now you switch from side by side to front and back. You smash, your partner moves forward to the T, slightly toward the side of your smash, to cut off blocks and drives.
why.good: Front is right. Shift a little more toward the side of the smash.

midcourt-gap.title: The mid-court gap
midcourt-gap.lesson: Against front and back, aim for the side mid-court: past the net player, in front of the back player.

steps.q: A at the net pushes into your mid-court. The shuttle arrives at shoulder height. Your opponents play front and back.
opts: Push into the side mid-court
Against front and back, the side mid-court is the gap: past the net player, in front of the back player. B has to come forward and hit from below.
Flat drive straight
Fast and flat, but B is waiting for exactly that.
Clear to the back
Safe, but you give them time and the attack.
Net shot
Right where A is waiting at the net.

flick-surprise.title: The surprise flick
flick-surprise.lesson: When the receiver stands right at the front and leans forward, the flick serve is a strong surprise.

steps.q: You are serving. The receiver A stands right on the service line and leans far forward. Which serve?
opts: Flick serve over A
A wants to attack the short serve and leans far forward. A flick over him catches him on the wrong foot. Very effective as a surprise.
Short serve to the T
The standard and never wrong. Against such an aggressive receiver, though, it has to be perfect.
Short serve wide
Opens an angle for A and is easier to attack.
High serve to the mid-court
Too short and too high: A smashes it straight away.

counter-drive.title: Counter the half smash
counter-drive.lesson: Answer a slow, flat half smash with a counter drive and take the attack back.

steps.q: A plays a slow, flat half smash. The shuttle arrives at shoulder height in front of you.
opts: Counter drive straight
A slow, flat half smash is an invitation. A fast drive straight past B takes the attack away from them.
Cross-court block to the net
Away from the smasher and the net player, so it is safe. But with this ball you could have put on more pressure.
Deep lift
You hand the attack back, even though the shuttle was attackable.
Straight net shot
B at the net gets there in one step and kills it.

close-smash.title: Smash from the mid-court
close-smash.lesson: The closer the smasher, the deeper you defend.

steps.q: Your lift was too short: B is in the mid-court and will smash from there. Place both of you for the defence.

why.best: The closer the smasher, the less reaction time you have. So defend deeper than usual, but stay side by side: your partner in line with the shuttle for the straight smash, you near the centre line.
why.good: The split is right. Take one more step back to gain time.

block-straight.title: Straight smash
block-straight.lesson: Against a straight smash, block cross-court: away from the smasher and away from the net player.

steps.q: A smashes straight from the back to your side. B has moved to the same side at the net.
opts: Cross-court block to the net
Away from the smasher at the back and away from B at the net. Both have to run far.
Deep cross-court lift
Safe, and A has to run diagonally. But you stay on defence.
Straight drive
Flies close past B, who can intercept it.
Straight block
Straight into the racket of B, who is waiting right there.

serve-base.title: Behind the server
serve-base.lesson: The server covers the net. The partner waits in the centre behind and covers pushes and flicks to the back.

steps.q: Your partner serves short. Tap where you should stand for the return.

why.best: Centred, behind the server, at about mid-court depth. Your partner covers the net, you cover pushes and flicks to the back. From the middle both back corners are equally close.
why.good: Close. Stand right in the centre so both back corners are the same distance away.

tape.title: Above the tape
tape.lesson: Above the tape, hit down. Below the tape, play a net shot or lift.

steps.q: A plays a net shot that floats too high. You meet it just above the tape. What do you play?
opts: Push down into the gap
Above the tape you can hit down. A quick push into the space between them forces a weak lift that your partner can smash.
Tight net shot
Not wrong, but you waste the chance to hit down. Save it for when the shuttle has already dropped below the tape.
Cross-court net shot
A long flight along the net gives A time to step across. A surprise option, but riskier than hitting down.
Lift to the back
You had the shuttle above the tape and turned it into defence for your team.

stay-front.title: Lifted over the net player
stay-front.lesson: The front player stays in front. Everything behind belongs to the back player.

steps.q: A lifts high over you to your back forehand corner. Your partner runs to take it. Tap where you should be.

why.best: Stay in front near the T, shifted slightly toward the shuttle side. Your partner attacks from the back and you take everything short. If you run back, the whole front court is open.
why.good: Right zone. Shift slightly toward the side your partner hits from: straight replies come back there.

lift-side.title: Defend after a lift
lift-side.lesson: After a lift, defend side by side. Against a cross smash, reply straight.

steps.q: Your partner was forced to lift to the back corner. B will smash. Place both of you for the defence.

why.best: Side by side, and the whole pair shifts toward the shuttle side. Your partner stands in line with the shuttle to cover the straight smash. You stand close to the centre line: the cross smash travels further, so you have more time and also cover the middle.
why.good: Right idea. Check the split: the straight defender in line with the shuttle, the cross defender near the centre line.

steps.q: B smashes cross-court at your forehand hip. Your reply?
opts: Flat drive straight
B is stuck in the far corner and A guards the net. A flat drive down your line flies past A into the empty mid-court. They lose the attack.
Straight block to the net
Safe and far away from the smasher. A can still reach it, so the block has to be tight.
Deep lift
Safe, but you hand them the attack again. Keep it for when you are late or off balance.
Cross-court block
The shuttle crosses right in front of A at the net. That is an easy kill.

smash-front.title: Attack after your smash
smash-front.lesson: When your team attacks, play front and back. Both of you shift toward the side of the smash.

steps.q: You smash straight from the back. Place yourself and your partner for the next shot.

why.best: Front and back. Your partner moves forward to the T, shifted toward the side you smashed, because blocks and drives come back there most often. You follow your smash a step forward but stay on the same side, ready for the next lift.
why.good: Front and back is right. Both of you shift toward the side of the smash, and you step forward after hitting.

drive.title: Flat drive battle
drive.lesson: In flat rallies, the first team to lift usually loses the attack. Stay flat or go short.

steps.q: A drives flat at chest height to you. Both opponents stand back in the mid-court. Your reply?
opts: Soft push into the forecourt
Both opponents are deep. A short, flat push into the space in front of them forces one of them to lift, and your team gets the attack.
Flat drive straight
Keeps the rally even. Fine, but it does not win you the attack yet.
High lift
You had a flat ball at chest height. Lifting gives them a free smash.
Half-high lift to the mid-court
Too short and too slow: the worst of both. They smash it from close range.

late.title: Late in the back corner
late.lesson: Red light: when you are late and the shuttle is low behind you, play high and deep to buy time.

steps.q: A pushes fast to your backhand back corner. You arrive late and the shuttle is already low behind you.
opts: High clear to the middle
You are late and off balance. A high, deep clear to the centre buys time to recover and gives the smasher less angle.
Straight high clear
Also fine, but if it falls short in their corner they smash straight back at you before you are set.
Backhand drop
From low behind you the drop is slow and floats. If it is not perfect, A at the net is waiting.
Cross-court drive
A flat cross from your deep corner passes right next to A at the net. Easy intercept.

attack-middle.title: High ball in the mid-court
attack-middle.lesson: Green light: attack the middle or the body.

steps.q: B lifts short to your mid-court. The shuttle is high in front of you. Where do you smash?
opts: Smash between them
The middle is the hardest spot to defend in doubles: both may go for it, or neither. The return also comes back central, where your partner waits.
Smash at the hip of A
Body smashes are hard to return well. A strong choice, just slightly easier to block than the middle.
Cross-court smash to the sideline
A longer flight gives B more time, and the straight block runs away from your partner.
Clear to the back
You had a high shuttle in the mid-court and gave the attack away.

cross-front.title: Front player after a cross smash
cross-front.lesson: The front player follows the shuttle: shift toward the side your partner hit to.

steps.q: Your partner smashes cross-court from the back. Place yourself (front) and your partner (back).

why.best: B will most likely reply straight, with a block or drive back down his line. That is your right side, so you shift toward it to kill the block or cut off the drive. Your partner recovers from the corner toward the middle of the back court, ready for a lift to either side.
why.good: Good shape. You shift more toward the side the smash went to, and your partner recovers to the middle of the back court.

deep-drop.title: Deep at the back
deep-drop.lesson: Yellow light at the back: when the shuttle is very deep, a fast drop keeps the attack better than a weak smash.

steps.q: B lifts very deep to your forehand corner. You get there, but the shuttle is slightly behind you.
opts: Fast, steep drop straight
From this deep, a smash arrives slow and flat. A fast drop keeps your team attacking and pulls them forward, where your partner waits.
Smash to the middle
Possible if you are strong at the back, but it is a long way and they can counter with a drive.
Clear to the back
Neutral and safe, but it gives them time. You lose the attack.
Slow cross-court drop
A long, slow flight across the court. A arrives early and kills it or plays a tight net shot.

t-serve-1-1.title: Receiving on the right
t-serve-1-1.lesson: In doubles, receive close to the front.

steps.q: A serves from the T. You receive in your right service court. Tap where you stand.

why.best: Close to the short service line, near the centre line. You attack the short serve early and still reach a flick.
why.good: Almost. Check how close to the line and the centre.

t-serve-1-2.title: Receiving on the left
t-serve-1-2.lesson: In the left court too, receive at the front near the centre line.

steps.q: A serves from the T. You receive in your left service court. Tap where you stand.

why.best: Close to the short service line, near the centre line. From here you attack short serves early.
why.good: Almost. Check how close to the line and the centre.

t-serve-1-3.title: Partner serves from the right
t-serve-1-3.lesson: The server’s partner stands in the centre behind.

steps.q: Your partner serves short from the right. Tap where you stand.

why.best: In the centre behind the server, at mid depth. Your partner covers the net, you cover pushes and flicks to the back.
why.good: Almost. Check how close to the line and the centre.

t-serve-1-4.title: Partner serves from the left
t-serve-1-4.lesson: Behind the server, stand in the centre, not behind one side.

steps.q: Your partner serves short from the left. Tap where you stand.

why.best: In the centre behind the server, at mid depth, so both back corners are equally far.
why.good: Almost. Check how close to the line and the centre.

t-serve-1-5.title: After your short serve
t-serve-1-5.lesson: After a short serve, stay at the front at the T.

steps.q: You have served short from the right. Tap where you wait for the return.

why.best: Right at the T, half a step forward, racket up. That way you reach net shots and pushes first.
why.good: Almost. Check how close to the line and the centre.

t-serve-2-1.title: Short serve too high
t-serve-2-1.lesson: Above the tape: flat and down into the side gap.

steps.q: The short serve rises too high. You meet it above the tape.
opts: Flat push into the side mid-court
Above the tape you play flat and down. The side mid-court, past the server and in front of his partner, is the gap.
Tight net shot
Safe, but you waste the chance to put pressure on at once.
Slow push at the server
The server is at the net and easily intercepts a slow push.
High lift to the back
Do not lift the return of a short serve; you hand over the attack.

t-serve-2-2.title: Short serve too high
t-serve-2-2.lesson: Above the tape: flat and down into the side gap.

steps.q: The short serve rises too high. You meet it above the tape.
opts: Flat push into the side mid-court
Above the tape you play flat and down. The side mid-court, past the server and in front of his partner, is the gap.
Tight net shot
Safe, but you waste the chance to put pressure on at once.
Slow push at the server
The server is at the net and easily intercepts a slow push.
High lift to the back
Do not lift the return of a short serve; you hand over the attack.

t-serve-2-3.title: Tight short serve
t-serve-2-3.lesson: Against a tight serve: flat into the side gap, never a short lift.

steps.q: The short serve is tight. You meet it just below the tape.
opts: Flat push to the side mid-court
The serve was tight. A flat push to the side mid-court finds the gap between server and partner.
Tight net shot
Good if it is really tight. But the server is right at the net.
High lift to the corner
Safe, but you have to defend straight away.
Half-high lift
Too short: the server’s partner smashes it from the mid-court.

t-serve-2-4.title: Tight short serve
t-serve-2-4.lesson: Against a tight serve: flat into the side gap, never a short lift.

steps.q: The short serve is tight. You meet it just below the tape.
opts: Flat push to the side mid-court
The serve was tight. A flat push to the side mid-court finds the gap between server and partner.
Tight net shot
Good if it is really tight. But the server is right at the net.
High lift to the corner
Safe, but you have to defend straight away.
Half-high lift
Too short: the server’s partner smashes it from the mid-court.

t-serve-2-5.title: Short serve too high
t-serve-2-5.lesson: Above the tape: flat and down into the side gap.

steps.q: The short serve rises too high. You meet it above the tape.
opts: Flat push into the side mid-court
Above the tape you play flat and down. The side mid-court, past the server and in front of his partner, is the gap.
Tight net shot
Safe, but you waste the chance to put pressure on at once.
Slow push at the server
The server is at the net and easily intercepts a slow push.
High lift to the back
Do not lift the return of a short serve; you hand over the attack.

t-serve-3-1.title: Receiver right at the front
t-serve-3-1.lesson: If the receiver stands right at the front, the flick surprises him.

steps.q: You serve from the right. The receiver A stands right at the front and leans far forward. Which serve?
opts: Flick serve over A
A stands right at the front, leaning forward. A flick over him catches him on the wrong foot.
Short serve to the T
Never wrong, but against such an aggressive receiver it has to be perfect.
Short serve wide
Opens an angle for A and is easier to attack.
High serve to the mid-court
Too short and too high: A smashes it straight away.

t-serve-3-2.title: Receiver far back
t-serve-3-2.lesson: If the receiver stands far back, serve short.

steps.q: You serve from the right. The receiver A stands far back in his service court. Which serve?
opts: Short serve to the T
A stands far back. A short serve to the T forces him forward to play from below.
Short serve wide
Also short and therefore good, but wide opens an angle.
Flick serve over A
A is already back and waiting for exactly that.
High serve to the mid-court
Too short and too high: A smashes it straight away.

t-serve-3-3.title: Receiver in a normal position
t-serve-3-3.lesson: The short serve to the T is the standard in doubles.

steps.q: You serve from the left. The receiver A stands normally, close to the service line. Which serve?
opts: Short serve to the T
Against a receiver in a normal position, the short serve to the T is standard: shortest path, little angle.
Flick serve over A
